content.text:
Connecting cfo.ai broke because of two separate things, and the first one was my doing.

**1. I switched it off.**
When I started the server for Chetan, I deliberately left `CFO_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` empty. I did that so the guest couldn't connect to cfo.ai. With that variable empty, the app turns the whole cfo.ai connection off. Its startup log says: `cfo.ai connection disabled: CFO_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID is not set`. That's why the "Connect cfo.ai" button on your screen doesn't work.

**2. Your cfo.ai registration points at `localhost`.**
- Connecting cfo.ai uses a login handshake (OAuth). During it, cfo.ai needs to know in advance which address it may send you back to after you approve.
- Your cfo.ai app was registered with `http://localhost:3000/api/cfo/callback` as that address.
- Now the app runs on `https://expansive-contents-five.ngrok-free.dev`, so the return address would be `…ngrok-free.dev/api/cfo/callback`. That doesn't match what cfo.ai has on file, so cfo.ai would refuse the handshake even with the setting on.

**What fixes it:**
- Register the app again with the ngrok address (`npm run cfo:register`), which gives a new client ID.
- Put the new ID in `.env`.
- Restart the server without blanking that setting.

**Why it was never an issue before:** you used `localhost`, which matched the original registration. It only broke because the app's address changed.

Nothing has been changed or registered yet. Do you want me to register it and restart? It adds a new app entry at cfo.ai and edits `.env`.

**No, not anyone can sign in, but the link is public and I found a weak spot.**

**What protects you**
- Public sign-up is turned off. A stranger can't create an account.
- Only users in `seed-users.json` can sign in.
- Sign-in attempts are rate-limited, which I hit myself earlier (HTTP 429). That slows down password guessing.
- Without a login the app is closed: chat and the other API calls return 401.

**What's exposed**
- Anyone who has the ngrok link sees the login page and can try passwords. The link will be in a Discord channel with many people in it.
- **Your `admin`, `alice` and `bob` accounts still use the example passwords** from `seed-users.example.json`. They're easy to guess, or someone can read them from the public repo. That's the risk: someone could sign in as **admin** on your public link and see your whole neatlogs project through the Neat Bot.
- The `mentor` password is random and 32 characters, so that one is fine.

**What I'd do before posting the link**
1. Change the passwords for `admin`, `alice` and `bob` in `seed-users.json` to long random ones.
2. Since the seed script won't change an existing user's password, remove those users and add them again. The sync script I just wrote can do that, but removing `alice` and `bob` also deletes their chat history. They look like test accounts, so that's probably fine. Chats for `admin` would go too.
3. A quicker option is to drop `alice` and `bob` from the file and leave only `admin` and `mentor`, and give `admin` a random password.
4. Share the link only in the #pink-chetan channel, not elsewhere.

Whether you register cfo.ai again doesn't change any of this. That registration only lets signed-in users connect their own cfo.ai accounts.

How do you want to handle the passwords? I'd suggest option 3 and generating the new admin password here, without printing it.

TASK A — rebrand "nlhack" to "Bot Company" everywhere in tracked files (use `git grep -n -i -E "nl ?hack|nlhack"` excluding the lockfiles first, then fix lockfile name fields too):
- User-visible text -> "Bot Company": web/index.html (<title> and meta description, e.g. "Chat with the Bot Company team of agents."), web/src/auth/LoginPage.tsx h1, web/src/shell/SidebarPanels.tsx (~line 278), src/auth/index.ts appName, src/cfo/register.ts client_name ("Bot Company CFO Bot").
- Package names: package.json "name" -> "bot-company", web/package.json -> "bot-company-web", and the matching "name" entries at the top of package-lock.json and web/package-lock.json (only those name fields; do not touch dependency data).
- Internal keys with the prefix `nlhack.` (RequestContext keys in src/mastra/workspace.ts and src/usage/turn-budget.ts; localStorage keys in web/index.html, web/src/App.tsx, web/src/lib/sidebar.ts, web/src/lib/tokens.ts) -> prefix `botcompany.` ; grep ALL usages so every reader/writer (including the pre-paint script in web/index.html and any tests) stays in sync. Telemetry workflowName in src/telemetry.ts -> "bot-company".
- Comments that say "nlhack:" / "nlhack motion tokens" etc -> "Bot Company". Do NOT rename the `rakazo-*` CSS classes/keyframes/variables (they are part of the adapted code) and do NOT touch the "Modified from rakazo (Apache-2.0), github.com/elie222/rakazo@912c977" one-line file headers. Check web/src/components/avatar/bot-avatar.tsx line ~549 ("Rakazo" text): if it is user-visible (title/aria-label/tooltip), change that visible string to "Bot Company"; if it is only a code comment, leave it.
- README.md: change the title "# NeatLogs Hackathon Project" to "# Bot Company" and replace the sentence "This project is being developed for the **NeatLogs Hackathon**." with "Built for neatHack 2026 (neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai)." Keep the quoted problem statement. Do not rename the directory or git remote.

TASK B — simplify the license/notice files, but stay Apache-2.0-compliant:
- The web UI contains code adapted from Rakazo (https://github.com/elie222/rakazo, Apache-2.0, commit 912c977). Apache-2.0 requires keeping the license text and the per-file "Modified from" headers, so DO NOT delete the Apache license text. Rename web/LICENSE.rakazo to web/LICENSE (git mv) and fix any references to the old name.
- Replace web/NOTICE (currently ~50 lines with a long file list) with a SHORT file (about 8 lines) stating: Bot Company web UI; parts are adapted from Rakazo (github.com/elie222/rakazo, commit 912c977), Copyright 2026 Rakazo contributors, Apache License 2.0 (see LICENSE in this directory); adapted files carry a "Modified from rakazo" header; the overall look and feel was inspired by Grok bot, and the UI design was built with help from looking at Grok's UI and designs. No file list.
- Add a short "Credits" section (3-4 lines max) near the end of README.md saying the same in plain words: inspired by Grok bot, built with help from looking at Grok's UI and design; web UI parts adapted from Rakazo under Apache-2.0 (see web/LICENSE, web/NOTICE).
- Check whether any other license-like file or long attribution block exists in tracked files (root LICENSE, package.json "license"/"author" fields, README sections) and report it; do not remove anything else without reporting.

VERIFY: `npm run typecheck`; `npm --prefix web run build` (this writes web/dist which the running prod server serves — that is fine); `git grep -n -i -E "nl ?hack|nlhack"` should only show things you intentionally left (list them); `git status --short`. 

Report (<250 words): list of changed files by category, anything intentionally left with "nlhack"/"rakazo", whether the web build and typecheck pass, and any risk you noticed (e.g. localStorage key rename resets saved UI preferences once; telemetry workflowName rename changes how neatlogs groups traces).

content.text:
A worker agent is doing both jobs now. It won't touch the running server, your data, `.env` or `seed-users.json`, and it won't commit anything.

**Rebrand to "Bot Company"**
- The visible names change: the browser tab title, the login page heading, the sidebar header, the app name in sign-in, and the name cfo.ai shows when you register ("Bot Company CFO Bot"). The cfo.ai registration I offered earlier will use the new name.
- Package names become `bot-company` and `bot-company-web`.
- The internal keys prefixed `nlhack.` become `botcompany.`, and the telemetry name becomes `bot-company`.
- The README title becomes "Bot Company", and the hackathon sentence becomes a short "Built for neatHack 2026" line.
- The repo folder and the GitHub repo are still called `nlhack`. I can't rename those from here, and nothing in the app shows them.

**License and credits**
- **Kept, trimmed:** the Apache license text stays, renamed from `web/LICENSE.rakazo` to `web/LICENSE`. The long NOTICE file with its list of copied files shrinks to about eight lines. The one-line "Modified from rakazo" headers in the source files stay.
- **Why not delete it all:** the web UI was adapted from the open-source Rakazo project, and its Apache 2.0 license requires keeping the license text and those notices. Removing them would break the license terms, and it would also be inaccurate to credit only Grok.
- **Your credit:** the short NOTICE and a new three-to-four-line "Credits" section in the README will say the project was inspired by Grok bot and built with help from looking at Grok's UI and design, plus the line about Rakazo.

**Side effects:**
- Saved UI preferences in the browser (sidebar width, theme) reset once, because their keys are renamed.
- neatlogs may list new traces under a different workflow name than the older ones.

When the worker finishes I'll rebuild, restart the server with the guest settings and check the link. I haven't done that yet, so the running site still shows the old name.
